title: Liveness, readiness, and startup probes that tell the orchestrator the truth
asA: platform operator running the service under Kubernetes
iWant: three probe endpoints that each answer their one question honestly and cheaply
soThat: the orchestrator restarts, routes, and rolls out instances on real signals

acceptanceCriteria.description: GET /healthz/live returns 200 with the specified response schema whenever the process can serve any request, and performs no dependency checks whatsoever.
acceptanceCriteria.given: a running instance with a deliberately unreachable database
acceptanceCriteria.then: it returns 200 against the specified schema, unaffected by the dependency outage

acceptanceCriteria.description: GET /healthz/ready returns 200 only when every declared downstream dependency check (database, cache, queues) passes.
acceptanceCriteria.given: an instance with all declared dependencies reachable
acceptanceCriteria.then: it returns 200 with the specified schema listing each check as passing

acceptanceCriteria.description: GET /healthz/ready returns 503 with a body enumerating the failed checks by name when any declared dependency is unreachable.
acceptanceCriteria.given: an instance with one declared dependency down
acceptanceCriteria.then: it returns 503 and the body names the failing check while still listing the passing ones

acceptanceCriteria.description: GET /healthz/startup returns 200 only after initialisation (migrations applied, cache warmed, config loaded) completes, and a non-200 with the pending steps before that.
acceptanceCriteria.given: an instance mid-initialisation and the same instance after initialisation
acceptanceCriteria.then: the mid-initialisation call is non-200 naming pending steps; the post-initialisation call is 200

acceptanceCriteria.description: All three probes sit outside the auth middleware and outside rate limiting: they succeed with no credentials and are never 401, 403, or 429.
acceptanceCriteria.when: each probe is called with no credentials at sustained frequency
acceptanceCriteria.then: every call is answered on probe semantics alone, never with an auth or rate-limit status

acceptanceCriteria.description: Probe requests do not appear in info-level request logs and are excluded from RED endpoint metrics; probe outcomes are recorded under their own dedicated metric.
acceptanceCriteria.given: a period of steady probe traffic
acceptanceCriteria.when: info-level logs and endpoint metrics are inspected
acceptanceCriteria.then: probe requests appear in neither, and the dedicated probe-outcome metric carries their results

acceptanceCriteria.description: Each probe's response schema and failure mode are documented in the generated spec: what a failure body contains and what an operator should conclude from it.
acceptanceCriteria.when: the three probe entries are read
acceptanceCriteria.then: each declares its success and failure schemas and its documented failure mode

acceptanceCriteria.description: Readiness reflects recovery: when a failed dependency becomes reachable again, /healthz/ready returns to 200 without a process restart.
acceptanceCriteria.given: an instance whose dependency outage has been restored
acceptanceCriteria.then: it returns 200 without the process having restarted
